title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 148 (Central Government to specify audit of items of cost in respect of certain companies)

content.overview: The Central Government may, by order, in respect of such class of companies engaged in the production of such goods or providing such services as may be prescribed, direct that particulars relating to the utilisation of material or labour or to other items of cost as may be prescribed shall also be included in the books of account kept by that class of companies. The Central Government may direct that the audit of cost records of class of companies covered under sub-section (1) and which fulfil the threshold limits as prescribed shall be conducted in the manner specified in the order. The cost auditor is appointed by the Board (on audit committee recommendation where applicable) and must not be the statutory auditor.
content.glance: Prescribed classes must maintain cost records; CG may direct cost audit by a cost accountant in practice; cost auditor is distinct from the statutory auditor.
content.study:
## Section 148 — Cost records and cost audit

**Cost records.** CG may order prescribed classes engaged in prescribed production or services to include specified cost particulars in the books of account.

**Cost audit.** CG may direct cost audit for covered classes that fulfil prescribed thresholds, conducted by a cost accountant in practice in the manner specified.

**Appointment.** Cost auditor appointed by the Board; where an audit committee is required, on that committee's recommendation. Remuneration determined as the section provides. The cost auditor must not be the statutory auditor under section 139.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Can the statutory auditor also be the cost auditor under section 148?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The cost auditor must not be the statutory auditor. Cost audit is additional to the statutory audit under section 139.
